Empirical Research Plan: Weather Shocks and Economic Activity  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Within-location panel difference-in-differences (two-way fixed effects) combined with an event-study distributed-lag specification.

Why it fits  
• Weather realizations are orthogonal draws from the local climate distribution ⇒ quasi-random shocks.  
• Two-way (location & time) fixed effects purge all time-invariant cross-sectional confounders (institutions, geography, long-run climate) and all global shocks common to every unit in a given year (oil prices, financial crises).  
• The event-study (leads & lags of shocks) lets us test for pre-trends (placebo leads) and trace dynamic adjustment paths that matter for long-run damage calculations.  

Mathematically (annual panel example)  
Y_{i,t} = Σ_k β_k TempBin_{i,t}^k + γ PrcpAnom_{i,t} + δ_i + τ_t + ε_{i,t}  

where i = spatial unit (district/county/grid cell), t = year (or month/quarter/day), δ_i = location FE, τ_t = time FE.  

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
Primary: “Hot shock” indicator equal to 1 if mean daily temperature in location i and time t exceeds the 90th percentile of that location’s 1950-1980 distribution (or, in degree-day form, cumulative DD above 29 °C).  

Secondary:  
• “Wet shock” = precipitation above 2 s.d. of local mean.  
• Extreme event dummies (cyclone wind speed > 64 kt within 50 km; drought SPI < −1.5).  

Control group  
The same location in periods that do not experience an extreme draw (i.e., Temp ≤ 90th pctl). Parallel-trends assumption is therefore “treated versus untreated years within the same location.”  

Timing / Event date  
Event date = first day (or month) in which the extreme threshold is crossed. Leads (t – 3 … t – 1) and lags (t … t + 3) will be entered separately in the event-study. No running variable is needed.  

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Randomness of short-run weather conditional on climate.  
Plausible; weather systems are chaotic and uninfluenced by local economic conditions at the spatial/temporal scale used.  

A2. Parallel trends (no differential pre-trends between would-be treated and untreated periods within a location).  
Plausible if macro shocks are absorbed by time FE; still testable via placebo leads.  

A3. No simultaneous unobserved shocks that are perfectly collinear with local temperature shocks (e.g., disease outbreaks caused by the same climatic conditions).  
Partly plausible; we mitigate by controlling for precipitation, humidity, and including location-specific linear trends.  

A4. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers across neighboring locations in same period).  
Questionable for energy markets or conflict. We will test robustness to spatial buffer exclusion and spatial HAC errors.  

================================================================  
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
T1. Measurement error in weather (sparse ground stations).  
– Use reanalysis & satellite products; validate against station data.  
– Spatially interpolate weather to centroids of economic units; aggregate to reduce noise (errors average out).  

T2. Adaptation/anticipation (planting decisions, migration).  
– Focus on short-run (≤ 1 year) responses, include leads to detect anticipation.  
– For agriculture, control for input use (irrigation, fertilizer) where available.  

T3. Spatial correlation in shocks → understated SEs.  
– Cluster at the weather-system level (e.g., state or 2° × 2° grid) or use Conley (1999) spatial HAC.  
– Block bootstrap by climate region as robustness.  

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast multiway FE regressions
library(conleyreg)   # spatially correlated SEs
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading ------------------------------------------------------------
econ  <- fread("economic_outcomes.csv")     # cols: id year gdp_yield mortality ...
weather <- fread("highfreq_weather.csv")    # cols: id year mean_temp mm_precip ...

# 2. Variable construction ---------------------------------------------------
# Merge
dat <- merge(econ, weather, by = c("id", "year"), all = FALSE)

# Local historical percentiles (1950-1980 baseline)
base <- dat[year %between% c(1950, 1980),
            .(p90_temp = quantile(mean_temp, .90, na.rm = TRUE)), by = id]

dat <- merge(dat, base, by = "id")

# Treatment indicators
dat[, hotshock := (mean_temp > p90_temp)]
dat[, prec_anom := (mm_precip - mean(mm_precip, na.rm = TRUE)), by = id]

# Leads & lags (event-study, here 3 leads/lags)
setorder(dat, id, year)
for (l in -3:3) dat[, paste0("hot_L", sprintf("%+d", l)) := shift(hotshock, l), by = id]

# 3. Main specification ------------------------------------------------------
# Example outcome: log agricultural yield
fe_formula <- as.formula(
  "log(agri_yield) ~ hot_L-3 + hot_L-2 + hot_L-1 + hot_L+0 + hot_L+1 + hot_L+2 + hot_L+3 + prec_anom | id + year"
)

est <- feols(fe_formula, data = dat, cluster = ~id)  # cluster on unit

# 4. Robustness: spatial HAC SEs --------------------------------------------
conley <- conleyreg(est, lat = dat$lat, lon = dat$lon, cutoff = 100, distance = "spherical")

# 5. Plot event-study coefficients ------------------------------------------
es_coef <- data.frame(
  leadlag = -3:3,
  beta = est$coefficients[grep("hot_L", names(est$coefficients))],
  se = est$se[grep("hot_L", names(est$coefficients))]
)
ggplot(es_coef, aes(leadlag, beta)) +
  geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = beta - 1.96*se, ymax = beta + 1.96*se)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -0.5, lty = 2) + labs(x = "Years from hot shock", y = "Log yield effect")
```

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
• Agriculture: Hot shock ⇒ −5 % to −15 % decline in yields (larger for rain-fed crops).  
• Labor & industrial output: decline of ~0.5 pp in annual growth per +1 °C average deviation above 29 °C.  
• Mortality: +0.4 deaths per 1,000 population for extreme heat weeks.  
• Energy: +2 % residential electricity demand per CDD above baseline.  
• Conflict & crime: 5–10 % higher incidence during hot or drought years.  

Direction: Generally negative for output & health, positive for energy demand & conflict.  

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (2-way FE / DiD)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
C1: No differential pre-trends (tested with leads) .............. 1  
C2: Exogeneity of treatment conditional on FE ................... 1  
C3: No interference/spillovers .................................. 0  
C4: Correct SEs for serial/spatial correlation .................. 1  
C5: Robustness across functional forms & alternative data ....... 1  

Total = 4 / 5 ⇒ credible but mindful of spatial spillovers.
